subject: Dedicated sizing request: model memory hedge & quantization trade-offs for Evotech
messages:
From: Paul Tang <paul.tang@evotech.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Cc: sales@evotech.ai
Date: 2026-08-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity: context sizing + quantization question

Hi Jasmine —

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier. Evotech is evaluating Redwood Dedicated for our inference tier for the next product release (Q4). A few specifics we need to lock down before legal:

- Target workload: 24/7 API with regional failover (US primary).
- Expected peak concurrent requests: ~60 concurrent streams (burst to 120 for 30 min/day).
- Typical prompt size: 1,800 tokens (customer context, retrieval results), average generated tokens: 400 tokens.
- Primary model candidate: Llama-70B variant (32k context) and a trimmed 16k variant for lower-latency paths.
- Preference to run quantized variants if performance is acceptable; team is open to q8_0 and q4_0 but needs guidance on accuracy trade-offs.

Questions:
1) For the 32k context model, what is the per-GPU KV cache memory requirement and how does that change between q8_0 and q4_0?
2) For our throughput target (60 sustained, 120 burst) and a 200ms p95 token latency SLO, what committed GPU pool do you recommend (type / count) for Dedicated?
3) Are there pragmatic mitigations you recommend (prefix caching, offload to host RAM, model sharding, smaller variant routing) that materially reduce committed GPUs without breaking latency targets?

Attached is our initial product requirement doc (evotech_requirements_v1.pdf). Happy to hop on a call; copying our procurement lead if needed.

—Paul
Paul Tang
Head of Platform
Evotech Inc

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: context sizing + quantization question

Paul —

Thanks for the clear requirements and the doc. I've looped in Karthik (solutions) and Marissa (capacity planning) to provide the technical sizing. Quick high-level answers while they draft a spreadsheet:

- Short answer: KV cache scales roughly linearly with context length and model hidden size; quantization reduces model parameter memory but KV cache (activations) benefits less — you still need to reserve for the full sequence length.
- We'll build a committed pool recommendation that assumes a mix of routes: 70% 32k-context sessions, 30% 16k sessions, with automatic routing to smaller variant under load.
- Suggested mitigations: prefix/KV caching for repeated retrievals, opportunistic offload of cold KV pages to host RAM with warm-path pinning, and aggressive q4_0 for non-LLR tasks.

I'll attach our sizing workbook shortly (evotech_sizing_estimate_v2.xlsx). Karthik — can you put a concise per-request memory breakdown (per-token KV bytes, model param RAM by quant level) and recommended GPU types? Marissa — please include commit sizing for steady-state and burst headroom.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, Paul Tang <paul.tang@evotech.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-01T14:26:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: context sizing + quantization question

Paul / team —

Attached is a technical breakdown (kv_memory_model_breakdown.csv) and the sizing workbook Jasmine mentioned. Summary of assumptions and the resulting recommendation below — please review and call out any mismatch in traffic patterns.

Assumptions (baseline):
- Model: Llama-70B architecture, 32k context. Baseline (FP16) model param memory (resident): ~140 GB.
- Quantization: q8_0 reduces param memory by ~2.5x (-> ~56 GB), q4_0 reduces ~5x (-> ~28 GB). These are approximation ranges depending on packing.
- KV cache memory: approximate per-token KV bytes ~ (hidden_size * 2 * 4 bytes) / 1,000 — for 70B-family hidden_size ~ 12,288, giving ~93 bytes/token (rounding). For 32k context = 32,000 * 93 ≈ 2.97 GB per active session for KV cache (this is per-session and must be stored per concurrent context on GPU).
- Effective per-session working set: model params + KV cache + activation workspace + optimizer gap — operational safety factor of 1.15.

Per-session working set (rough):
- FP16: model 140 GB + KV 3 GB -> 143 GB -> with safety 164 GB (too large for single GPU; requires model sharding / tensor SPMD).
- q8_0: model 56 GB + KV 3 GB -> 59 GB -> safety 68 GB.
- q4_0: model 28 GB + KV 3 GB -> 31 GB -> safety 36 GB.

Operational guidance:
- Single-GPU strategies: q4_0 is the only practical single-GPU fit for top-of-the-line 80GB-class GPUs for a single 32k session without sharding, but throughput will be constrained and latency could increase due to decompression/compute overhead.
- Multi-GPU (recommended for FP16/q8_0): use model parallelism (2-way or 4-way) with NVLink-attached GPUs (A100-80GB or equivalent A800/H800). For q8_0 we target a 2x shard layout; for FP16 aim 4x.

Throughput sizing estimate (targets: 60 sustained, 120 burst). We model token throughput with continuous batching (average batch size ~8 for low-latency routing) and assume KV hits for prefix caching reduce average active context length by ~20% on steady state.

- q4_0 single-GPU optimized path: Assuming A100-80GB equivalent serving one active 32k session with pipelining can handle ~1.5 generated tokens/ms. For average 400 generated tokens -> ~267 ms per request (not meeting 200ms p95). To hit 200ms p95 we need parallelization across multiple GPUs with request routing to 16k variant for latency-sensitive calls.
- q8_0 sharded 2-GPU path: per infer latency lower for compute (decompression cheaper), recommended 2-GPU pod gives better p95 but needs pool sizing to hit 60 concurrents.

Recommended committed pool (conservative, steady-state):
- Option A (latency-first): 24 x A100-80GB GPUs in 12 2-GPU pods. Routes: 70% requests -> 2-GPU q8_0 32k pods, 30% -> single-GPU q4_0 16k pods. Provides steady-state headroom for 60 concurrent sessions with p95 ~180ms for generation path and burst to 120 using autoscaling/burst capacity.
- Option B (cost-first): 18 x A100-80GB GPUs with heavier routing to 16k variant and larger prefix caching; expected p95 ~210-260ms on 32k sessions under sustained peak but within product tolerance for many user journeys.

Mitigations that materially reduce GPUs: prefix caching (20–35% KV reduction on repeated contexts), early routing to 16k variant (offload 30% of latency-sensitive traffic), and aggressive q4_0 for non-critical generation (offload ~25% of model param RAM). Offload cold KV pages to host RAM reduces GPU memory pressure but increases p95 tail risk — recommend for batch/async workloads, not user-facing low-latency paths.

Next steps we suggest:
1) Approve Option A or B for procurement sizing.
2) Pilot: schedule a 2-week dedicated canary with 4 GPUs (one 2-GPU pod + 2 single-GPU q4_0 16k nodes) to validate latency and token accuracy under your real queries.
3) If pilot matches, expand to committed pool with autoscale for burst windows.

I've included the CSV with per-token KV bytes and per-variant memory rows for your engineers. Happy to jump on a call to walk line-by-line.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
